items.line: vorkommende דיה wird (Chulin 63, b) mit איה identisch genommen, so
items.note: Deut 14:13 has the extra bird דיה, which is absent from Leviticus; Chulin 63b identifies it with איה. דאה appears in Lev 11:14, so it cannot be the word found only in Deuteronomy.

items.line: Man unterscheidet 1) ביעי דרכרא (Beza 7, a), Eier durch Hahnen-
items.note: Beza 7a has ביעי דדכרא, 'eggs of the male', i.e. fertilized by the cock, matching 'Eier durch Hahnentritt'. דכרא means 'male'; דרכרא is not a word.

items.line: מורוח (Chulin 64, b); nur jene erstgedachten Eier sind brütfähig. —
items.note: Chulin 64b uses the known term ביצים/ביעי מוזרות for wind-eggs (unfertilised eggs). מורוח is not a word and comes from the common ז/ר and ת/ח confusions.

items.line: בבגיא, oder כפאגי (so liest Muskato für das corrupte גובא) genannt;
items.note: The bird is the parrot, Arabic babbāghā' (cf. 'Papagei'). The g sound favours כפאגי over כפאני, but Muskato's exact emendation is uncertain, so this is a likely rather than certain reading.

items.line: geien andere Namen. Dort heißt es: Der Vogel שבור אנדרפטא ist
items.note: The Chulin 62b bird name seems to be read שבור (with ב) before אנדרפטא; I recall this but am not certain. Reading B swaps ב for כ and its span also takes in the following word.

items.line: zu essen erlaubt, der Vogel פירוז אנדרפטא ist zu essen verboten. Aruch
items.note: 'Aruch liest beide Male: אנדרפטא' implies the Talmud's second occurrence differs, so the 'verboten' bird likely reads אנדרפחא. The ט form matches the Greek -φατος etymology and the Aruch reading. This is an inference, not certain.

items.line: In Babylon erlaubt man den Vogel קקותא zu essen; in Me-
items.note: Chulin 63a reads קקותא (Babylon) and תחוותא (Eretz Israel). קקותא also fits the comparison with κικκάβη. Reading B's קקיוא is not a word.

items.line: Unter dem im vorhergehenden Artikel erwähnten קקותא werden
items.note: קקותא has a normal Aramaic -תא noun ending and fits a bird named in Chulin 63a. קקיוא does not look like an attested form, though I can't confirm the exact spelling from memory.

items.line: große Kautz, und קואי nach Abwurf der Reduplication der kleine
items.note: Removing the reduplication from the main form קקואי gives קואי. The form קיאי would instead come from Aruch's variant קיקאי, so A is likelier but not certain.

items.line: (oder קריא) im Traume, ist wegen seiner Häßlichkeit von böser Vor-
items.note: Lev. 11:17 has כוס (with samekh), and the Targum renders it קדיא. The ם in reading A is an OCR confusion of final mem for samekh.

items.line: mudstelle derselbe durch ייבנ"ץ, Hibou erklärt. Mit dem franz. Worte
items.note: ייב"ץ fits Rashi's Old French gloss for 'hibou' (nominative ibouz), parallel to the ייב"ן form cited for Lev. 11:17. The extra נ in ייבנ"ץ looks like an OCR insertion rather than a printed form, but I cannot confirm this from Rashi's text.

items.line: wie auch zu Lev. 11, 16 durch אישפריויר, Épervier, Sperber. In-
items.note: Old French 'espervier' fits אישפריויר (es-pr-e-v-ie-r) as in the passage text. B's אישפרויר is also a plausible spelling, and both forms of the 'ostour' word are possible, so this is not certain.

items.line: Chulin 42, a heißt es: Der נץ würgt kleines, der גם großes
items.note: The Talmudic bird here is גס (OCR renders final ס as ם). Aruch's variant גז keeps the initial ג, so the first letter is ג, not נ; נם is not a word.

items.line: hingegen würgt Hühner und Gänse. — Aruch liest jedoch גז für גם
items.note: Chulin 42a contrasts נץ with גס (read here as גם), and Aruch's variant is גז. Both words begin with gimel, as in the surrounding lines, so B's נז נם is not a word.

items.line: Jonathan, der Lev. 11, 13 עזניה durch בר גוא*) übersetzt; allein
items.note: Mussaphia cites Jonathan to support Aruch's reading גז, so the printed word was probably בר גזא. Reading B keeps the ז, reading A keeps the ג. Each is one look-alike error away from גזא, so this choice is a guess.

items.line: ten der 10 Bußtage (angef. in den Tos. Chulin ibid. s. v. דריפת)
items.note: The selicha phrase should be מדרס (trampling), and B has the correct final ס where A's מדרם is a likely ם/ס confusion. B's נז is probably a misreading of גז, and the lemma ending (דריסה vs דריסת) is uncertain, so both readings have errors.

items.line: liest: מדרם גז ונץ; Jesaias Pick liest aber in letzterer Stelle: מדרם גם
items.note: Reading A's ג in גז/גם matches the preceding line's 'גז ונץ' and Pick's two bird names (גז = falcon, גם = vulture), whereas B's נז/נם are not known words. However, מדרם is probably a misread of מדרס ('trampling'), which B has right, so neither reading is fully correct.

items.line: In Midr. Jalk. Schim. 2. Th. fol. 114, d ist wohl בר גזין für בר זגין
items.note: The passage is about גז as a bird of prey (falcon), so the emendation בר גזין derives from גז. Reading B, נזין, has no link to the discussion.

items.line: In Midr. Jalk. Schim. 2. Th. fol. 114, d ist wohl בר גזין für בר זגין
items.note: Lewysohn proposes reading בר גזין in place of the corrupt בר זגין, an emendation by transposing the first two letters. זגין is the letter-swapped form of גזין; וגין gives no such sense.

items.line: ber gegenüber mit Recht גם (Groß), da er noch einmal so groß wie
items.note: The gloss (Groß) means 'large', which is Hebrew גס, as in נץ גס for the larger hawk in Hullin and the poskim. גם means 'also' and does not fit; a final mem misread for samekh is a common OCR error.

items.line: בר חיריא? Es ist, wird geantwortet, der שורינקא (Würger). Hier
items.note: Chulin 63a explains בר חיריא as שרינקא, the usual Talmud spelling, so B is likely. The plene variant שורינקא is also attested, so this is not certain.

items.line: er auch בואי, von dem erzählt wird, daß David einst ging den בואי
items.note: Sanhedrin 95a reads 'לשכר בזאי', which Rashi takes as a place name and others as 'Beute' (from בזה, spoil). בזאי is also linked to Persian/Arabic baz 'falcon', matching the falcon section. בואי makes no sense here.

items.line: und so dürfte die Erklärung des Aruch: בואי als Vogelname zu halten annehm-
items.note: The passage ties the bird to Arabic/Persian baz and Syriac bz' (falcon), so the Aruch's word must share the root b-z: בזאי. The reading בואי has ו in place of ז, a common look-alike error, and breaks that connection.

items.line: יתירה (Chulin 61, a). Der Verfasser des ספר הבריה**) schreibt ohne
items.note: The book is Sefer ha-Berit (ספר הברית) by Pinchas Eliyahu Horowitz, an encyclopedic work that covers natural history. "הבריה" is not the title of any known book, so reading B is what Lewysohn printed.

items.line: bemerken, daß der gemeine Adler, איגלא, Aigle, eine Hinterzehe hat
items.note: Tosafot usually spell Old French 'aigle' with a double yod for the 'ai' sound, which would give אייגלא. I can't verify the printed text, so this is a guess.

items.line: gum עוניה durch עוז, oder אוז wiedergiebt, so kann das letztre Wort
items.note: עוז matches the paired variant אוז ('oder אוז') as a Targumic rendering of עזניה. עזא is also plausible as an Aramaic form, so this is not certain.

items.line: gel דיו ein Stück Fleisch vom Markt nahm und es in einen Garten
items.note: Raschi's gloss 'והוא לשון דיה' implies the Talmud's word is an Aramaic form related to דיה, so דיי fits. דיו normally means 'ink'. I could not verify the exact Talmud text and am partly guessing.

items.line: Vogel, den man Vulture (Geier) nennt, gleichbedeutend mit ריה." —
items.note: The biblical bird is דיה (Deut 14:13, the dayyah, a kite or vulture), and rabbinic sources identify it with the ra'ah. Lewysohn is glossing a vulture name as equivalent to this bird. ריה is not a bird name and looks like a ד/ר OCR confusion.

items.line: im Anhang s. v. ירודוח gehandelt wird.
items.note: ירודות has a normal Hebrew plural ending (-ות). ירודוח is not a recognizable word, so it is likely an OCR confusion of ת with ח. I could not verify the exact headword in Lewysohn's appendix.

items.line: so muß entweder in unserer Raschistelle zum Talmud סום für עגור
items.note: Jer 8:7 lists סוס ועגור (swift and crane). The emendation therefore puts סוס in place of עגור, and סום is not a word.

items.line: Vogel, die eigentliche דיה רגונית (grausame דיה, s. Art. Storch),
items.note: Chulin 63a calls the anafah a 'dayah ragzanit' (irritable/angry bird). רגזנית, from רגז 'to be angry', fits the gloss 'grausame' and the following explanation of anger. רגונית is not a word.

items.line: Chulin 63, a heißt es: Der Vogel אריכי שקי וירוקי, welcher
items.note: Chulin 63a reads the Aramaic plural phrase אריכי שקי וירוקי, and the parallel plural אריכי requires the plural form וירוקי.

items.line: מורומא. Hierzu Raschi: Es giebt von dem Vogel שקיטנא zwei Ar-
items.note: The same passage later prints the bird name as מורומא, which supports reading A for Chulin 63a. However, ו/י confusion is common in OCR and both spellings are plausible variants.

items.line: tete und als rein allgemein bekannte Vogel מורומא. Dieses letztre
items.note: The same word appears as מורומא elsewhere in the passage (lines 2 and 8), which favours that spelling here; this matches the Chullin 62b tradition (מורוומא/מורומא). Talmud spellings vary, so this is not certain.

items.line: und מורומא als identisch und nur als Provincialismen zu nehmen;
items.note: The marked line pairs שקיטנא with מורומא, the same word the passage uses twice above. Reading B is a merger of a variant spelling with האנקה, which comes from the next line.

items.line: Chulin 63, a wird gesagt, daß der gemeine Flamingo (שקימנא,
items.note: Lewysohn glosses it 'kurz und roth', so the word is Aramaic גוצי ('short'); נוצי does not fit. The bird name in Chulin 63a is, as I recall, שקיטנא (Jastrow lists it under that spelling).

items.line: durch צינניה, Cigogne. Es fragt sich nur, wie der Talmud den
items.note: Rashi's Old French gloss for חסידה is ציגוניא (cigonia, 'cigogne'). צינניה is not a known form and looks like a misreading of ג as נ and of the final letters.

items.line: dessen, daß דיה, oder דיו (B. mez. 24, b, vergl. ob. §. 196) nur
items.note: B. mez. 24b has the Aramaic דייתא (kite), so a form with double yod (דיי…) fits better than דיו.

items.line: Schwingen schwarz ist, kann mit Recht ריה לבנה „der weiße hoch-
items.note: Chullin 63a identifies the stork (חסידה) as דיה לבנה and the heron (אנפה) as דיה רגזנית. The bird name is דיה, from דאה 'to soar'; ריה is not a bird name.

items.line: seiner Wildheit ריה רגונית „der grausame hochschwebende Vogel“ heißt.
items.note: The Talmud (Chullin 63a) names the heron דיה רגזנית, the 'angry kite', which matches 'grausame'. The kite דיה is also the bird called hochfliegend; ריה is not a word, and רגונית is a misreading of רגזנית (ז read as ו).

items.line: Dem Namen ריה לבנה entspricht vollkommen ריה חיורתא, dessen
items.note: Reading A matches the spelling ריה used in the surrounding lines and the standard Talmudic spelling חיורתא. The Rashi gloss (corrupt for ולטור) is uncertain in both readings.

items.line: bar corrupt für ולטור, wie ריו zu B. mez. 24, b; aber auch wesent-
items.note: Neither reading fits the sentence clearly. ר/ד and ס/ד are common OCR confusions; חסר ('lacking', i.e. a defective spelling of the gloss) is marginally more plausible than דיו חסד ('ink, kindness'), so this is a guess.

items.line: zens (§. 38) heißt er auch: קורקיר (Baba batra 23, a), wegen seiner
items.note: Baba Batra 23a names the raven קורקור, an onomatopoeic word for its croaking that fits 'wegen seines Krächzens'. קורקיר is not an attested word and comes from a ו/י confusion.

items.line: Andere übersetzen לוך durch λοπός, Zwiebelschalen.
items.note: The Greek λοπός means husk or peel, and לוף is its direct transliteration, matching 'Zwiebelschalen'. לוך does not correspond to the Greek, so it is a ף/ך misreading.

items.line: ticum. — Hiermit vergl. man den Verf. des מחנת כהונה (zu Midr.
items.note: The commentary on Midrash Rabbah (here on Esther) is מתנות כהונה, 'Mattenot Kehunah', by Issachar Ber Ashkenazi. מחנת is not a word in this title, with ח misread for ת.

items.line: אין שני זרזורים ישינים על דף אחד „Zwei Staare schlafen nicht auf
items.note: The standard rabbinic word for starling is זרזיר (e.g. 'לא לחנם הלך זרזיר אצל עורב'), whose plural is זרזירים. However, a variant spelling זרזור exists, so A cannot be ruled out.

items.line: Der erste jener acht Vögel ist der חוכא, in welchem ich die
items.note: The passage contrasts this bird with חוגא in the next article, which fits a similar-sounding חוכא. I cannot confirm the exact spelling in the Chullin bird list, so this is a guess.

items.line: art bezeichnet. חוכא, von חכא „verbergen“, mag entweder das Ver-
items.note: The Hebrew/Aramaic root for „verbergen“ is חבא (to hide), so the bird name derived from it is חובא. חכא carries no meaning of hiding.

items.line: רק"ק פ"פ „Der Vogel, der im Deutschen Lerche heißt, ist, wie ich
items.note: The phrase is "אב"ד דק"ק פ"פ", i.e. av beit din of the holy community (ק"ק) of Frankfurt, with the prefix ד. That matches the German "Rabbiner zu Frankfurt"; "רק"ק" is not a word here.

items.line: Wort סיג heißt Zaun, und davon סוגה Umzäunung; möglich also,
items.note: The familiar rabbinic word for 'fence' is סייג (Avot 1:1, 'עשו סייג לתורה'). The defective spelling סיג is also possible in print, so this is a guess.

items.line: Der vierte jener acht Vögel ist der הרנוגא (Chulin 62, b).
items.note: The next line breaks the word down as הר + נוגא, which requires the form הרנוגא. This matches the Chulin 62b bird name. הרנתא does not fit that etymology.

items.line: Das Wort mag aus הר „Berg“ und נוגא (im Sinne von נגה,
items.note: The bird is הרנוגא (Chulin 62b), so the component after הר is נוגא, matching the preceding line. Reading B's נתא does not fit this word.

items.line: Der fünfte jener acht Vögel ist der כוחילנא (Chulin 62, b),
items.note: Lewysohn takes this Chulin 62b bird name from כחל, 'black paint'. כוחילנא fits the usual Aramaic -נא form of these bird names; the extra yod in B is a common OCR slip. Talmud texts may differ, so this is uncertain.

items.line: 2. S. 380), wovon die größere wohl הרנגולא „Hahn“ und die klei-
items.note: The Aramaic for 'Hahn' is תרנגולא and for 'Henne' is תרנגולתא. The forms with ה are an OCR confusion of ת and ה and are not words.

items.line: מררא „widerspenstig“, „wild“ genannt wurde, mag der wilde
items.note: 'Widerspenstig' (rebellious) is Aramaic מרדא, from מרד, and the cock is spelled תרנגולא. Reading A's מררא and הרנגולא are ד/ר and ת/ה misreadings.

items.line: Angabe. Als Aequivalent für den verbotenen Vogel גירוחא ist die
items.note: Chulin 109b reads 'asar lan girutha, shara lan lishna de-kavra', i.e. גירותא and כוורא (Aramaic 'fish'). Reading A's ח for ת and its כורא are OCR look-alike errors.

items.line: aufzählt, gerade גירוחא und כורא unerwähnt läßt; ein Gleiches ge-
items.note: גירותא with ת is the more plausible Aramaic form, and כוורא is an attested spelling; גירוחא is not a known word. This rests on form alone, not a verified source reading.

items.line: Der letzte jener acht Vögel ist endlich der הושלמי (Chulin 62, b),
items.note: Lewysohn splits the alternative spelling into הל and שמי ('Öde, Steppe'), so the final yod is required. That makes הושלמי / הלשמי the printed forms; B drops the yod and loses this etymology.

items.line: „Schutthaufen“, und שמי „Öde, Steppe“, und ich möchte hier die
items.note: Lewysohn splits הלשמי into הל + שמי, glossing the second part as „Öde, Steppe“. So שמי, as in reading A, is required, and B's שם is a truncation.

items.line: brauchte תמתי einmal (fol. 12, col. d) mit schön und das zweite
items.note: Song of Songs 5:2 and 6:9 apply 'יונתי תמתי' to the dove, and Midrash Shir ha-Shirim Rabba glosses that word as both 'schön' and 'vollkommen'. The word Lewysohn prints is therefore תמתי; תמה is not the biblical form.

items.line: Das Fettgekröse des Rindes heißt כנחא, was Münster (im Lex.)
items.note: The second word is most likely בוניא, the Talmudic bird name Lewysohn uses in the next line, which supports A. The first word, כנחא vs כנתא, is genuinely uncertain.

items.line: Chulin 102, b heißt ein unreiner Vogel קלניתא, was Raschi
items.note: The bird in Chulin is קלניתא, and the passage repeats that same spelling two lines later. The ending -ita is a normal Aramaic form, while -יחא is the typical ת/ח OCR confusion.

items.line: Κηλὸν heißt mager, trocken, und so mag קלניתא, wie פרוא
items.note: Chulin 102b names the bird קלניתא (qalanita); the same spelling appears earlier in the passage, and קלניחא is a ת/ח misread.

items.line: 20, a sagt Raschi: die קלניתא ist so mager, daß sie kein Mensch ißt.
items.note: The bird in B. Batra 20a is spelled קלניתא, as in Jastrow's entry for a small bird. קלניחא, with ח for ת, is not an attested word.

items.line: wird eines Vogels gedacht, der כעין קלניתא „wie die קלניתא“, d. i.,
items.note: The Bava Batra 20a bird name is קלניתא, with the normal Aramaic feminine ending ־יתא. קלניחא is not a known word and reflects a ת/ח misread.

items.line: chem er die Speise bewahrt. — Vergl. Anhang s. v. אם הים
items.note: 'אם הים' ('mother of the sea') reads as a plausible bird-name entry in the Anhang. 'את הים' (accusative particle plus 'the sea') is not a lemma. I could not confirm the actual entry.

items.line: Nach Jalk. Schim. 2. Th. fol. 13, d soll dies der טוס, Pfau, sein.
items.note: 'Pfau' (peacock) is rabbinic טווס, the usual spelling and Lewysohn's likely heading form. The defective spelling טוס also occurs, so A remains possible.

items.line: ren nicht. Wir haben schon früher (§. 201) שקי als Benennung
items.note: The plural 'Füße der Vögel' fits the Talmudic plural form שקי (legs) better than the singular. The singular שק appears in the next sentence as the root 'Schenkel', but here both readings remain possible.

items.line: Chulin 62, b wird der Vogel מונא חמרא (Gemischter Wein) zu
items.note: The gloss 'Gemischter Wein' points to Aramaic מזגא חמרא ('mixed wine'), the Chulin 62b form. מוגא matches it except for ו/ז, a common OCR confusion. מונא would need a second error, ג read as נ. Neither reading is exactly מזגא, so this is not certain.

items.line: Chulin 62, b wird gesagt, daß der Vogel בת מונא חמרא (Toch-
items.note: I faintly recall the Chulin 62b bird name as בת מוגא חמרא, but my memory is unsure. ג/נ look alike in print, so this is a guess.

items.line: ter des מונא חמרא, s. §. 232) zu essen gestattet ist. Bei Aristoteles
items.note: Chulin 62b reads בת מוניא חמרא, which Lewysohn spells מונא, as in the previous line's citation. The ג/נ confusion makes B a likely OCR slip.

items.line: Chulin 62, a heißt es: Der Vogel מרדו זגיד ואכיל ist zu essen
items.note: Chulin 62a sets זגיד ואכיל (permitted) against סגיד ואכיל (forbidden), a parallel pair of verbs. וגיד has no sense here.

items.line: Chulin 62, b wird der Vogel צרדא als reiner Vogel erklärt.
items.note: Chulin 62b names the clean bird צרדא, which Jastrow glosses as 'linnet' (Hänfling). ערדא is not this bird name.

items.line: Chulin 62, b wird der Vogel ברדא (Aruch liest: בר ארא) als
items.note: Aruch's variant likely just splits the text's ברדא and keeps its ד (בר אדא); ר and ד are often confused in OCR, so this is a guess.

items.line: 502) der צפרתא gegenüber gestellt, ähnlich der Entgegenstellung bei-
items.note: The OCR text of the passage itself shows צפרתא and then צפורתא, with no yod. That matches reading A. Both spellings are possible in Aramaic, though, so B cannot be ruled out.

items.line: zu sticken pflegte. Jedenfalls bezeichnet צפורתא alle Arten von klei-
items.note: The first line of the passage prints צפורתא, the defective spelling usual in Lewysohn's 1858 typesetting, so the same form is most likely repeated here. ציפורתא is an equally valid plene spelling of the same word, and the two differ by an added yod rather than a look-alike letter, so this is not certain.

items.line: wird verschieden erklärt, von Raschi zu B. mez. 24, b durch גוזלות,
items.note: Both words occur in the passage, and A matches the printed spellings: plene גוזלות (Rashi, B. mez. 24b) and פרדריש (Perdrix, Rashi to Berachoth 39a). Reading B's defective spelling and abbreviation-style פרדי"ר don't fit this text.

items.line: פריגין (vergl. auch Tos. Chulin 62, b. s. v. כרזי). — Ein anderer
items.note: Chulin 62b discusses young birds, and I recall a bird name כרוי in that sugya, which Tosafot would gloss with פריגין. I can't recall כרזי as a bird name.

items.line: Vergl. Burdorf (Lex. p. 1846), und צלצלא, vergl. §. 252.
items.note: Both spellings are attested for this Aramaic bird name (cf. §. 252), and the readings differ only by a plene yod. I lean to the defective spelling צלצלא as the likelier printed form, but this is a guess.

items.line: טוס (B. Kama 55, a) טוס (Sabbat 130, a), und in der Parallel-
items.note: Reading A gives valid spellings of the peacock word (טוס/טוסא). Reading B's middle token ט ות is broken, though its טווס may be the actual first form; the printed text may mix spellings.

items.line: zur ersten und letzten Stelle das Wort durch פוואן, Paon übersetzt;
items.note: פוואן renders Greek pavo/Paon (peacock), as the passage states, and טוסמ belongs to the feminine form (Greek taôs). Reading B is fragmentary and has letters missing.

items.line: אוז (B. mez. 91, b), אווזא (Joma 84, a*), pl. אוזין (Sebachim 70,
items.note: Reading A is printed: אווזא matches the later citation "von אווזא", and אוזין is the plural Lewysohn gives. קוקא fits the "Quacken" etymology and the plural קאקי. Reading B has a broken word (א זין) and קיקא, which is not the goose word.

items.line: (im Tischbi) sagt: „Von אוז ist der Pl. אוזים, von אווזא ist der Pl.
items.note: Levita derives the plural אוזים from the singular אוז ('goose', the headword of this section); אז ('then') is not the goose word.

items.line: (im Tischbi) sagt: „Von אוז ist der Pl. אוזים, von אווזא ist der Pl.
items.note: The passage's own headword line, 'אווזא (Joma 84, a*)', uses the double-vav spelling, and Levita's quote refers back to that same form. So אווזא / אווזות / אווזאות is the consistent reading. The single-vav forms are also valid spellings, so this is likely rather than certain.

items.line: Arab. وز und إوز, und so ist אווזא wohl richtiger als אווזא.
items.note: The sentence contrasts two spellings, so reading A's identical pair cannot be what was printed. Reading B at least shows two different forms, the single-vav אוזא matching Arabic وز / إوز. But B's first token is garbled, so neither reading fully matches the print.

items.line: C. 8. H. 7) findet sich die Redensart: כרון אחון קקו פריפט „Ihr
items.note: כדון ('now') is the common Yerushalmi Aramaic word, so reading A's כרון looks like a ד/ר OCR error. The second word was probably printed as אתון ('you'), which neither reading gives exactly, so this is a guess.

items.line: C. 8. H. 7) findet sich die Redensart: כרון אחון קקו פריפט „Ihr
items.note: This is likely Greek περίπατος, 'walking', as in strutting or gabbling geese walking in a line, which fits פריפט. פריפס gives no clear word, but I am working from memory of the Yerushalmi passage, so this is not certain.

items.line: gedacht. Die Flaumfeder (כלומא, Pluma, die aber richtiger מלס,
items.note: The gloss 'Pluma' supports פלומא, the Aramaic loan from Latin pluma, over כלומא. But B's אזז is not a word, while A's אוז (goose) is plausible. מלס versus מלט for 'Molasse' is also unclear, so the evidence is mixed.

items.line: Gans einen kürzern Schnabel als die zahme. Obwohl קויה, sowohl
items.note: The Talmudic passage (B. Kama 55a) on the wild vs. tame goose uses Aramaic קועיה, 'its neck', which Raschi glosses as 'bec'. I recall it as spelled with ע, but קויה could be a variant spelling, so this is not certain.

items.line: In dieser Stelle heißt es משחא דגרפא דאווא; dahingegen in der
items.note: B's דנגרפא is not a word, so A's דגרפא is right. However, דאווזא in B is the usual Talmudic spelling. A's spelling דאווא matches the parallel quotation in the next line, so the print may have used it, but this is uncertain.

items.line: Parallelstelle A. Sara 28, a: משחא דאווא בגרפא דאווא, was Raschi erklärt:
items.note: Reading B's כנגרפא is not a word. Reading A, משחא דאווא בגרפא דאווא, is a well-formed phrase with ב- 'with' (matching Raschi's gloss 'smeared on with a goose feather'). Its spelling דאווא also matches the preceding line.

items.line: das Sprüchwort: שפיל ואזיל בר אוזא ועיניה מטייפי „Es bückt sich
items.note: Megilla 14b has the proverb 'ועיניה מטייפי', and Lewysohn translates 'ihre Augen', which fits ועיניה. The form ועיניהו is less natural, but some printings vary, so this is not certain.

items.line: dünnen Teig zu einer Speise bereitet (Tos. ibid. s. v. טפל), sonst
items.note: טפל ('to coat', here with thin dough) matches the Tosafot heading at Pesachim 74b and fits the German sense. שפל חזא is not a plausible lemma here.

items.line: sammenlaufen (צומח הגידין, §. 73), und gestattete hierauf die Vögel
items.note: The Talmudic term is צומת הגידין, 'the junction of the sinews', which fits Lewysohn's 'where the thigh veins run together'. צומח means 'growing' and makes no sense here.

items.line: 17, a), ferner שכוי (R. ha-Schana 26, a), נרגול (Sanhedrin 63, b)
items.note: Sanhedrin 63b cites Nergal (2 Kings 17:30) as the god of the Cuthites, explained as the rooster (תרנגולא). The printed form is נרגול/נרגל; נרנול is not a word, just a ג/נ OCR confusion.

items.line: und גבר (Joma 20, b). — Die Henne heißt תרנגולה (Beza 2, a),
items.note: Beza 2a speaks of 'תרנגולת העומדת לאכילה'. The standard rabbinic form for the hen is תרנגולת, with ת and ה being a common OCR confusion.

items.line: גברית (Sabbat 67, b*) und wird von Einigen סכוה genannt (San-
items.note: Sanhedrin 63b explains סכות בנות (2 Kings 17:30) as a hen (תרנגולתא), so the word is סכות. סכוה is an OCR confusion of ת and ה.

items.line: heißt וגתא (Bechoroth 8, b). Sie heißt ferner ihres Schreiens
items.note: In Bechoroth 8b (R. Joshua and the Athenian elders) the brooding hen is called גזא, which Rashi glosses as a hen. גתא is not attested with this meaning.

items.line: Taches; dahingegen erklärt Raschi (Sanhedrin 105, b) סורייקא durch שורות
items.note: Raschi glosses the word as שורות שורות (lines), a variant of שורייקא, and it is linked to Arabic סוריאק. That fits סורייקא; פורייקא is not a known word.

items.line: נוקיש und erklärt es durch Fadenweise; er fügt hinzu, daß im Arab. סוריאק,
items.note: סוריאק matches the Aramaic סורייקא and renders the Arabic شراك (shirāk) given right after it. פוריאק is not a plausible form; פ is a misreading of ס.

items.line: — גוזל (s. §. 1, Anm. ***) heißt sowohl die junge, als auch die
items.note: Lewysohn spells the word plene throughout the passage (בר גוזלא, גוזל בן שנה), matching the biblical spelling for 'young dove'. The defective form גזל would instead read as 'robbery'.

items.line: Schwarz: חוצאות הארץ pag. 6), oder als Personenname nach dem
items.note: Joseph Schwarz's geography of Palestine is titled תבואות הארץ, and 'Totzaot' is a known variant rendering of it. תוצאות is a real word ('outcomes, borders'); חוצאות is not a word.

items.line: (קוביש, Couvées) herabnahm (Berachoth 44, a); doch ist hier
items.note: Both spellings are plausible, so this is a guess. The form with a single yod, קוביש, seems the more likely printed form. The Bavli text of Berachoth 44a that I can recall reads בריכות ('broods'), which does not settle the spelling here.

items.line: dies that hieß ארא (Raschi אשחלין, Stellionat, Sanhedrin 25, a).
items.note: Rashi glosses it with the Old French Old French 'eschaillons' (decoys/lures), transliterated אשחלין. A final ז in אשחליז is not a plausible word ending and is a typical ן/ז OCR confusion.

items.line: stimmt werden kann, ist die unter dem Namen ראציפי (Chulin 62, a),
items.note: Aruch's variant is attested as דריציפי (A); B's דייציפי looks like an OCR corruption. ראציפי for the Chulin 62a form is less certain.

items.line: wird das Ei der צינילתא (fem. von צילצלא) als Bezeichnung eines
items.note: Jastrow lists ציצילתא as the feminine of ציצלא, a small bird, citing Shabbat 80b ("ביעתא דצ׳"). This matches the passage's egg-as-small-object usage, so B is the attested pair. A's forms look like misreadings (צ read as נ, and an inserted ל).

items.line: Turteltaubenart wird kaum einen Fuß lang, demnach muß צינילתא
items.note: The Talmud (Shabbat 80b) has ביעתא דצינילתא, a small bird that Rashi glosses as עוף קטן. Lewysohn treats it as the feminine of צילצלא, which matches reading A; reading B's ציצילתא is not the attested word.

items.line: Ibid. 62, b werden die תורין של רחבה mit den כפשני צוציני identi-
items.note: The Talmud (Chulin 62b) has כפשני צוציני. The same word is spelled צוציני again later in this passage, so the doubled-yod צוצייני looks like an OCR artifact.

items.line: von תורים, während das Wort צוציני verschieden erklärt wird. Ra-
items.note: The passage spells the word צוציני in its other occurrences, including the earlier citation and Aruch's explanation. The Talmudic form (Chullin 62b, כופשני צוציני) has no double yod, so צוצייני is a spurious variant.

items.line: gen giebt Aruch (s. v. צץ) folgende Erklärung: למה קורין איתן צוציני?
items.note: Aruch's question 'why do they call them…' needs אותן ('them'), so B's first word is right; איתן ('strong') makes no sense here. But B's צוצייני conflicts with the spelling צוציני used elsewhere in the passage, so neither reading is fully clean.

items.line: man sie צוציני? Weil sie Locken am Kopfe haben, wie es (Ezech.
items.note: Reading A matches the Aruch quotation on the line just above, which spells it צוציני, and the German translation most likely repeats that spelling. Reading B is not impossible, since the doubled yod spelling also occurs, so this is not certain.

items.line: Stelle der חורין, wohl aber an der der בני יונה zum Opfer genommen
items.note: The sacrificial doves are תורים (Aramaic/Mishnaic plural תורין), paired with בני יונה as the two kinds of birds fit for offering. חורין ('free men' or 'holes') makes no sense in this context.

items.line: גמל (Gen. 15, 9) durch: חסילא בר יון, ebenso גוזליו (Deut 32, 11)
items.note: Gen. 15:9 reads "ve-tor ve-gozal" (a young bird), so the word is גזל. Targum Jonathan renders it as a young dove (חסילא בר יון), which parallels גוזליו in Deut. 32:11. גמל (camel) does not fit.

items.line: גמל (Gen. 15, 9) durch: חסילא בר יון, ebenso גוזליו (Deut 32, 11)
items.note: Deut 32:11 reads על גוזליו, spelled with vav, and חסילוי is the correct Aramaic plural with the 3rd-person suffix ('his young'). The B forms drop these letters.

items.line: die Erklärung Samuels (Rabba batra 75, a) von ציצלא durch חאציל;
items.note: Lewysohn calls the word a corruption of חסיל. חאציל, with its initial ח, fits that remark; האציל would be a less obvious corruption. I could not verify the exact text of Bava Batra 75a.

items.line: wilde Taubenart, der Erstere übersetzt es durch שבנינא, und die
items.note: The Targum to Ps 84 renders דרור with שפנינא, the Aramaic word for a wild dove. Neither reading has פ, but שבנינא is closer, since ב and פ alternate. The print may actually read שפנינא.

items.line: ist die סנינית לבנה (weiße Schwalbe), so sind סנונית*) und צפור דרור
items.note: The word for swallow is סנונית. The passage itself prints סנונית לבנה later, so סנינית is an OCR confusion of ו and י.

items.line: sowohl am Hause (כבית) als auf dem Felde, was allerdings von
items.note: The German gloss is "am Hause", and בבית means "in the house". The Talmudic discussion (Beza 24a, Shabbat 106b) says the bird dwells בבית as well as in the field, so בבית is the printed word. כבית ("like a house") does not fit the gloss.

items.line: unserer Talmudstelle ferner: מעליא דכילהו שיכלי גריעא דכילהו שליו „Der
items.note: The Aramaic for "of all of them" is דכולהו ("the best of all of them"), so B fits the German gloss "von ihnen". דכילהו is not a word; the ו was misread as י.

items.line: Rabba (Schemoth fol. 142, b), wo es mit רשנת בשמן identificirt wird*).
items.note: The phrase is דשנת בשמן, from Psalm 23:5 ('you anoint my head with oil'), which the Midrash uses to gloss שליו as fatness. רשנת is not a word.

items.line: Der Pl. von שליו ist שְׁלָיִים (Jozar zu Sabbat ha-Gadol s. v. אמיר),
items.note: The passage itself gives the plural as vocalized שְׁלָיִים, and it cites the piyyut as 's. v. אמיר' without a vav. B's שלוים ואמיר contradicts both.

items.line: erstens פסיון (B. Kama 55, a; Joma 75, b), pl. כסיוני (Kiduschin
items.note: The singular is printed as פסיון (pheasant, Greek phasianos), so the plurals should also begin with פ. כסיוני comes from the common OCR confusion of פ with כ.

items.line: endlich wird gesagt: Mancher Sohn ernährt seinen Vater mit כסיוני
items.note: The passage is about the word פסיון ("pheasant"). The saying "מאכיל אביו פסיוני" (Kiddushin 31a, Yerushalmi) uses the plural/construct form פסיוני. The reading כסיוני confuses כ and פ and is not a word.

items.line: rung von סלין (§. 260), wonach jene vier Vögel wegen ihrer Schmack-
items.note: סליו fits as a samekh spelling of שליו (quail), the word of the Yoma 75b passage on the 'four kinds of quail'. סלין gives no fitting sense here.

items.line: מכלל הצומח כי הוא חי ומתנועע אינו מחליף מקומו כי הוא נעוץ והקיע בארץ
items.note: The phrase "נעוץ ותקוע בארץ" means "stuck and fixed in the earth", a standard paired expression. "והקיע" is not a sensible word in this context.

items.line: das Gesetz gestattet nur 4 Arten zu essen, nämlich סלעם, חרגל, ארבה
items.note: The marked line lists the four permitted locust kinds from Lev. 11:22: סלעם, חרגל, ארבה, חגב. חרגל is the second of these. למינו is the qualifier "nach ihrer Art" that appears on the following line, not one of the names in the list.

items.line: und חגב, fügt aber zu ארבה den Nachsatz למינו (nach ihrer Art) und
items.note: Lev. 11:22 reads ארבה למינו, and the marked line attaches the Nachsatz 'nach ihrer Art' to ארבה. למינהו ('nach ihren Arten') belongs to the other three kinds on the next line.

items.line: col, 442) nach Vorgang Ibn Esra's von רבו „viel sein“, wobei an
items.note: Lewysohn derives ארבה from the root 'to be many'. רבו is a real verb form ('they were many') that fits 'viel sein'; רבי ('my master'/'Rabbi') does not fit this meaning.

items.line: ungeschwänzt (Tos. Chulin 65, b s v. לא) — Den Namen גוביי er-
items.note: גובי matches the biblical locust name (Amos 7:1, Nahum 3:17) behind the talmudic גובאי, and the Yerushalmi's גבו etymology fits it. גוביי is a less usual spelling but could be a variant, so this is not certain.

items.line: beim Anblick der גוביי der Segensspruch: ברוך דיין האמת gesprochen werde.
items.note: Lewysohn probably kept the Yerushalmi's own spelling for 'locusts', which seems likely to be גוביי, a variant of the Bavli's גובאי. Neither form can be ruled out.

items.line: übrig, daß in beiden Talmudstellen צפורת כרמים eine reine Heu-
items.note: This is the term צפורת כרמים from Mishnah/Talmud Shabbat (90b), a locust-like insect. The defective spelling צפורת is common in print and likely what Lewysohn used, but the plene ציפורת is a legitimate variant, so this is a guess.
